title: Pegasus Infra / Redwood Partner Intro & Discovery
next_steps: Sofia to send partner intro deck and pricing template
Daniel to propose tech deep-dive and benchmark plan
Pegasus (Maya) to share infra diagram and expected QPS/latency targets
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive week of 2026-12-15
Exchange NDA and partnership MOU draft
action_items: Sofia: send partner deck and pricing template - due 2026-12-13
Daniel: draft benchmark plan and list of telemetry requirements - due 2026-12-16
Maya: share VPC design, region preferences, and expected p99 latency targets - due 2026-12-12
Zoe: provide SOC2 / ISO contact and initial questions - due 2026-12-14
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Pegasus Infra to explore integration for joint go-to-market and potential GPU/cloud reselling. Key topics: deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security / compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC), latency/cost tradeoffs, benchmarking plan, and next steps to run a pilot and schedule deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on partners, i have Daniel and Priya with me, we can do quick intros.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, Liam here, head of partnerships at Pegasus, thanks for the time.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Maya, cloud architect, i'll be the tech lead on our side.
[00:20] Daniel Cho: Daniel, solutions engineer, hi.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Ravi, product, quick question up front, are we focusing on reseller model or integration?
[00:28] Sofia Martinez: Great question. Today is discovery, we want to understand Pegasus' go-to-market and technical constraints; we see multiple paths -- reseller, co-sell, or deep OEM embed.
[00:34] Maya Chen: From infra side we run multi-region GPU clusters, mainly A100/H100 class, we also partner with third party GPU chassis. We're interested in a managed inference stack that can connect to our billing and provisioning.
[00:45] Priya Singh: That's helpful, do you have an existing API or marketplace integration pattern?
[00:50] Maya Chen: We have a marketplace and APIs, yes. We also have internal customers who want private tenancy, VPC peering, and KMS integration for keys.
[01:00] Daniel Cho: Ok that maps well to Redwood offerings: hosted API for quick onboarding; Dedicated for reserved capacity; and Private (VPC/On-prem) for regulated workloads. How strict are the tenancy and data residency requirements?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Some of our customers are banks — need VPC-only, no shared tenancy, and KMS/HSM for key management. Audit logs and SIEM integration also required.
[01:22] Zoe Alvarez: Security here, we also need proof of SOC2 and details on data retention and audit log retention, is that something you can share?
[01:30] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely, we can share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs; we'll send the docs after the call.
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: On the business side, what are typical margins / partner pricing? Are you flexible on reseller discounts?
[01:45] Sofia Martinez: We have partner tiers and reseller discounts — i'll share the partner deck and pricing template. For pilots we often do credits and co-marketing support.
[01:52] Ravi Patel: Technical question: latency constraints — some customers are p99 < 200ms for shorter prompts, others prioritize throughput and batch. How does Redwood handle latency vs cost tradeoffs?
[02:03] Daniel Cho: We tune using routing policies, dedicated pools for low latency, and batching/caching for cost. Also quantization and model variants help. For p99 <200ms, typically Dedicated instances pinned to H100s or low-contention hosting works best. There's always a tradeoff but we can benchmark to your workloads.
[02:20] Maya Chen: Can you run within our VPC or do you require outbound traffic to your control plane?
[02:25] Priya Singh: For Private deployments we can run a customer-managed control plane in your VPC; for Dedicated we can do VPC peering and private links. Some customers opt for on-prem package for air-gapped.
[02:36] Zoe Alvarez: How about keys, do we get customer-controlled KMS?
[02:39] Daniel Cho: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations.
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: Any references in financial services?
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: We have a few mid-sized banks and enterprise customers with SOC2/ISO requirements — we'll include anonymized reference notes.
[02:52] Maya Chen: For the benchmark, we need to test a few models — foundation models and some LLM variants — and measure p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens. Can Redwood provide a benchmark harness?
[03:03] Daniel Cho: Yes, we have a benchmark harness and runbooks; we'll propose a plan: 1) share infra and workloads, 2) Redwood runs pilot on Dedicated/dev cluster, 3) measure latency/throughput/cost, 4) share results and tuning recommendations.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: What telemetry do you need?
[03:20] Daniel Cho: Request/response timestamps, model versions, prompt sizes, concurrency, and error rates; if you can provide sample prompt sets that helps.
[03:30] Maya Chen: We'll redact PII and provide representative workloads.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: On product integration, we'd like an easy provisioning API so our customers can enable Redwood as an option in the Pegasus marketplace. Does Redwood have automation APIs for provisioning tenants and billing hooks?
[03:45] Priya Singh: We have APIs for tenant ops, model pins, and routing policies, plus webhook-based billing events. We can share our API spec.
[03:53] Zoe Alvarez: Liability and data residency — do you offer contractual language for data handling and breach notification?
[03:59] Sofia Martinez: Yes, our enterprise contracts include data handling clauses; legal can share standard language and we can negotiate for big customers.
[04:07] Maya Chen: Another concern: model weights and IP. If we resell, customers sometimes want to run models within our hardware, not cloud. Is on-prem supported?
[04:15] Daniel Cho: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployments with a customer-managed control plane. Model weights can be hosted in your environment. We have a secure model onboarding process.
[04:24] Liam O'Connor: Great. Any specific integrations with GPU vendors or hardware partners we should know about?
[04:29] Priya Singh: We work with popular hardware stacks, optimize kernels per architecture, and have documented performance profiles for H100/A100 and others; we can share verified performance profiles.
[04:38] Ravi Patel: Competitors question — how are you different from Lambda or a self-managed stack?
[04:42] Sofia Martinez: Main difference is our production-first developer experience and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with built-in routing, caching, and rollout tooling. We also emphasize cost-aware controls and monitoring.
[04:55] Maya Chen: For the pilot, timeline? We want something early Q1 2027 ideally. Can you commit to that schedule?
[05:02] Daniel Cho: Seems feasible — pilot scoping in December, setup and benchmark in January, validation in early Feb. We'll align on capacity.
[05:10] Sofia Martinez: Ok to summarize next steps: I'll send partner deck, pricing, SOC2 and security docs; Daniel will propose a technical deep-dive and benchmark plan; Maya will share infra topology and workloads. We'll schedule the deep-dive week of Dec 15.
[05:24] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good.
[05:26] Maya Chen: Quick question — any gotchas on network egress or VPC peering? We need details for our security team.
[05:33] Daniel Cho: We'll include network requirements and typical firewall rules. Also notes on NAT, private link, and peering.
[05:39] Zoe Alvarez: We'll also send our preliminary security questionnaire.
[05:43] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and drop the docs in the shared drive.
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
[05:51] (meeting ends)
